writer.markdown:
## Company overview

Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) designs, develops, manufactures, leases and sells electric vehicles, as well as energy generation and storage systems, in the United States, China and internationally. It reports two segments, Automotive and Energy Generation and Storage. Beyond vehicle sales, it sells automotive regulatory credits and offers non-warranty maintenance, collision and insurance services, parts and retail merchandise. Within the Auto Manufacturers industry and the Consumer Cyclical sector, it carries a market capitalization of $1.46T, with shares at $370.59 against a 52-week range of 297.38-498.83.

## Financial commentary

Revenue rose from $81.46B in fiscal 2022 to $96.77B in 2023 and $97.69B in 2024, then eased to $94.83B in 2025. Net income followed a weaker path: $12.58B in 2022 and $15.00B in 2023, then $7.13B in 2024 and $3.79B in 2025. The result is a net margin of 3.7% and a return on equity of 4.7%, which suggests profitability has compressed even though the top line has held broadly steady. The data also show trailing revenue growth of 25.5%, which contrasts with the recent annual revenue figures and should be read with care. Debt/Equity is a low 0.18.

## Comps commentary

On the primary measure, Forward P/E, Tesla trades at 171.6 against a peer median of 8.8, a premium of +1841%. The trailing P/E of 346.3 compares with a peer median of 21.5 (+1508%). EV/EBITDA of 133.6 is +655% above the peer median of 17.7, and EV/Revenue of 13.9 is +1324% above a median of 1.0. Revenue growth of 25.5% is +1242% relative to the peer median of 1.9%, and Tesla's 3.7% net margin sits against a peer median of -3.9%. Leverage is the exception, with Debt/Equity 84% below the peer median of 1.15. The peer group of General Motors, Ford, Toyota, Rivian and Li Auto is mixed, with several multiples unavailable, so the median should be treated cautiously. The gap indicates the market is pricing in expectations well beyond those of traditional automakers.

## Risk commentary

The most severe risks, each rated 3, begin with production ramp delays and manufacturing cost control, where problems launching products or controlling costs could pressure already narrowing margins. Dependence on EV demand and adoption of autonomous driving is similarly central to future growth. Tesla also faces intensifying competition from established and new rivals, and it is heavily reliant on Elon Musk as CEO. Rated 2 are supplier delivery, pricing and quality failures, and evolving laws that could impose costs or prohibitions. Recent news is partly relevant to the demand risk, with headlines noting European demand boosting Q3 deliveries, while an anticipated Roadster reveal relates to product launch execution.
